title: Correlation: when everything falls together
desc: Why owning many similar assets is still one bet

cards.title: Five stocks, one bet?
cards.situation: You own 5 stocks. All five are big tech companies. Are you well diversified?

options.feedback: The count looks good, but the same news hits all five. When tech falls, they fall together.

options.text: Not really: they tend to move together
options.feedback: Same industry, same news, same moves. You own one bet five times.
Big companies fall too. And when tech has a bad month, all five big tech names usually fall at once.

cards.work: Tech sell-off: all five fall around 20% together. Five stocks, one bet.
cards.added: Feedback for C written for the Academy

cards.title: Correlation
cards.text: **[[correlation|Correlation]]** shows how two assets move together. Assets that rise and fall as one don’t protect each other.

blocks.tip: Mix things that don’t all move the same way: different industries, countries and asset types.

cards.title: A bad month for tech
cards.text: Two tech stocks and a bond fund, through the same sell-off.

items.title: 6 weeks
items.label: Over six weeks Tech A falls 14%, Tech B falls 20%, the bond fund rises about 2%

cards.foot: The two tech stocks fell as one. Bonds often hold steadier in a sell-off, though not always.

cards.title: More stocks, more safety?
cards.reality: 20 stocks in one industry is still one bet. And in a real crash, most stocks fall together, so even a wide spread of stocks drops.
cards.rule: count the different kinds of risk, not the number of stocks.

cards.title: Pick the best pair
cards.q: Which pair is most likely to spread your risk?

options.feedback: Two banks face the same rates, rules and news. Stocks and bonds are different asset types that often move differently.
Two oil companies rise and fall with the same oil price. That’s one bet twice.

options.text: A stock fund and a bond fund
options.feedback: Stocks and bonds are different asset types, and they often move differently.
Two chip makers ride the same chip cycle and the same tech news, so they tend to move together.

cards.title: High correlation
cards.q: Two assets have a high correlation. That means they…

options.feedback: High correlation means they rise and fall together, so they give each other little protection.
Opposite moves are negative correlation. High correlation means they rise and fall together.
No clear link is low correlation. High correlation means they rise and fall together.
Assets that move together don’t protect each other. When one falls, the other usually falls too.

lines: Correlation: how two assets move together.
Same industry often means the same moves.
In a crash, most stocks fall together.
